full_text:
The National Weather Service has extended a heat advisory for most of the Bay Area to last through at least Wednesday, tacking on two extra days for residents to be mindful of extreme temperatures.
The NWS announced Saturday that an initial Monday heat advisory for the interior Bay Area and Central Coast — which covers most of the region’s population save for some living along the Sonoma, Marin, Peninsula and Santa Cruz coastlines – would need to be prolonged.
Some of the highest forecasts through the extended heat advisory period, which ends at 10 p.m. Wednesday, include temperatures approaching 100 degrees in Concord for most of the week, Livermore and Hollister hovering in the high 90s, and San Jose, San Rafael and Napa hitting the mid-90s.
According to the weather service, people need to be mindful of effective cooling and adequate hydration during the heat wave, “shift outdoor activities to cooler times of the day,” and keep pets and people out of unattended vehicles.
No red-flag warnings have been issued, but forecasters did warn of “elevated fire weather conditions” in higher terrain in the region. There is a Spare the Air alert effective through Sunday, but no additional alerts were declared for the newly extended heat advisory period as of Saturday afternoon.
